A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RePlan work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, tables, and figures. Renumbered and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original IV-Edit evaluations, planner and training ablations, global-rephrasing comparisons, attention analyses, and bounding-box perturbation results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a human preference study, latency measurements, another backbone evaluation, and MagicBrush and SmartEdit results.

M1.justification: Section 5.3 adds a rule-group attention acceleration variant using per-token bitsets and fused, on-the-fly visibility computation instead of storing a dense mask. This changes attention execution while preserving the planner, five visibility rules, and two-stage GRPO objectives.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix H adds evaluation on MagicBrush and SmartEdit, extending coverage beyond IV-Edit to their more constrained, locality-focused editing scenarios. The existing IV-Edit composition and training-data sources remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 adds Flux.2-Klein-9B to Table 1. Tables 6–7 introduce HIVE variants, MagicBrush-tuned InstructPix2Pix, MagicBrush, InstructDiffusion, and SmartEdit-7B comparisons. Table 3 additionally compares accelerated RePlan with unaccelerated RePlan and multi-turn Kontext. Earlier comparison methods are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include a blinded study of 100 randomly sampled pairs with 12 experts, randomized output ordering, and majority voting; latency comparisons across one to five regions and different attention implementations; and external-benchmark evaluations using their respective metrics and annotation-derived region-guidance controls. Existing IV-Edit scoring and training settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds acceleration ablations and region-count scaling measurements in Table 3, contrasts full RePlan with annotation-guided attention injection in Tables 6–7, and adds many-region editing case studies in Figures 7, 10, and 11. Earlier planner, reasoning, training-stage, attention-rule, overlap, and perturbation analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new human-study voting protocol and preference percentages do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New results include the Klein comparison, with Overall scores of 3.45 without RePlan and 3.92 with it; human preferences of 35% RePlan, 15% Kontext, and 50% ties; and five-region latencies of 54.1 seconds accelerated versus 113.8 unaccelerated and 221.0 multi-turn. Tables 6–7 add external-benchmark scores. Matched earlier numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 5.3 introduces mathematical definitions for group-membership and visibility bitsets, their bitwise visibility condition, and a memory-complexity argument reducing explicit-mask storage from O(n²) to O(n ceil(k/W)) machine words. Existing method equations and reward definitions are unchanged.

C1.justification: The framework, small-data GRPO, and IV-Edit contributions remain central. v2 strengthens the conclusion with an explicit claim of improvements across MMDiT backbones without compromising efficiency, and Appendix D adds a first-of-its-kind claim for coherent parallel editing across numerous regions.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting dense masks to attention-kernel overhead and latency growth to longer text sequences. Appendix H interprets external results as task-domain generalization and expands discussion of CLIP metric misalignment. Appendix D adds arguments about alternative editing approaches' locality and coherence limitations.

D1.justification: v2 specifies FlexAttention, fused visibility testing, bitset storage, and the attention implementations used for timing. Earlier training-data construction details and the project-page address remain. Hardware and detailed training hyperparameters are still not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Gemini 2.5, GPT-4o, FlashAttention, FlashAttention-2, FlexAttention, DiT, and latent diffusion. Appendix D adds novelty positioning against cut-and-paste, layer-based, inpainting, and ControlNet approaches. The main related-work account otherwise remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites and expands the benchmark rationale, introduces numbered benchmark and ablation subsections, and adds appendix contents, keywords, and acknowledgements. It removes the short LLM-polishing disclosure. Most existing methodological and analytical prose is retained.

P2.justification: The document adopts substantially different typography, margins, running headers, and float placement. Earlier Tables 2–3 are merged; Table 1 gains shaded RePlan rows; new latency and benchmark tables and three multi-region figures are added. Existing qualitative panels are retained despite relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's reliance on IV-Edit and automatic judging: two external benchmarks, a blinded human study, and controlled latency comparisons directly support generalization, instruction following, and efficiency. The gains are not uniform: MagicBrush CLIP-T decreases from 0.2913 for Kontext to 0.2866 for RePlan, qualifying the broad improvement language. Missing timing hardware and uncertainty estimates limit interpretation, but the added complementary evidence provides a substantial net quality improvement.
